definition: Temporal annotation is the study of how to automatically add semantic information regarding time to natural language documents.
details: It plays a role in natural language processing and computational linguistics.

explainer.lead: Temporal annotation is the study of how to automatically add semantic information about time to natural language documents. It matters within natural language processing and computational linguistics as the bridge between raw text and machine-usable time.

tiers.eli5: It is the work of teaching computers to tag the time information in written text.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to mark up documents with time-related meaning for NLP pipelines. The available facts give no specific tools, standards or pitfalls.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as the study of automatically adding semantic information regarding time to natural language documents; it plays a role in natural language processing and computational linguistics. No formal definition or limits are given.

explainer.example: A document is annotated so its time references carry machine-readable temporal meaning for later processing.
